newsitem.title: JAPAN: North Korea says disappointed over New York talks.
newsitem.headline: North Korea says disappointed over New York talks.

text.p: North Korea on Sunday said the results of the preliminary four-way talks held in New York last week were disappointing, and warned the United States against using North Korea's dire food shortage as a political weapon.

"The results of the 5th-7th August preliminary meeting held in New York are, in a nutshell, below our expectations," the North Korean news agency KCNA, monitored in Tokyo, quoted a North Korean spokesman as saying.
He said that thanks to North Korea's efforts, tentative agreement had been reached on issues including the level of participants, the venue and procedures for four-way talks.
"However, there were raised seriously conflicting views on some key issues such as the agenda," KCNA quoted the spokesman as saying.

Three days of preparatory talks in New York last week failed to reach final agreement on procedures for substantive negotiations planned for Geneva and involving the United States, China, South Korea and North Korea.

On Friday, the United States said a "significant" disagreement was over whether the agenda should be specific or general, and said the U.S. does not want to negotiate a U.S. withdrawal of troops from the Korean peninsula.

The North Korean spokesman said a main principle of the talks was that they should not cover the internal affairs of North Korea, but issues which include a peace agreement between the U.S. and North Korea and the withdrawal of U.S. troops from the Korean peninsula.

"The United States, however, refused to accept such issues as agenda items and insisted on generalising the agenda items so that other issues can be discussed. We suspect that the U.S. intends to avoid its responsibility and interfere in internal affairs of our nation," he said.

"What also disappointed us was the U.S. position that food assistance to North Korea can be expanded only after the four-way talks are opened. With (a) serious food problem, we guard against possible use of food assistance to the North Korea as a political weapon," the spokesman said. "The U.S. attitude at the preliminary meeting added fuel to our fear," he added.
He said, however, that since Washington had come to the negotiating table, "although belatedly," North Korea would "watch their attitude for some more time".
